prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor kitchen scene with a ceiling, two hanging pendant lamps above, a background wall with cabinets and a bright window about 3.5 to 4 metres away, a doorway and adjoining room further back on the right, and two standing people in front of the camera wearer. In frame 1, the person on the right in a white top is roughly 1.5 to 1.8 metres away and closer than the person on the left in a dark t-shirt at roughly 2.5 to 3 metres, with the two standing about 1 to 1.5 metres apart; across frames 1 to 5, the left person approaches to within about 1.8 to 2 metres (growing larger and brighter relative to the background) while turning his head downward toward the counter area between them, and in frame 5 the camera wearer's own right hand and forearm enter the bottom-right foreground within 0.3 to 0.5 metres (arm's reach), partially occluding the lower body of the right person while a foreground counter surface on the bottom-left also enters within arm's reach (~0.5 metres). Both people have their lower bodies below the waist cut off by the bottom of the frame and the foreground counter, and the left person partially occludes the upper-left kitchen cabinet and window frame as he moves closer. The depth map clarifies the continuous distance gradient along the ceiling, hanging lamps, and dark background wall that are either blown out by the window glare or lost in shadow in the RGB strip, and clearly separates the foreground silhouettes from the recessed kitchen wall. However, the map is unreliable in its relative brightness scaling across frames—as the very close foreground counter and camera wearer's arm enter in frames 4 and 5 at maximum brightness, the automatic depth normalization darkens the two people and the hanging lamp even though neither person retreats.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates two foreground people standing side-by-side in front of the camera wearer—one on the left in a dark shirt (progressing from ~2.8 metres to ~1.8 metres away) and one on the right in a white top (~1.5 to 1.8 metres away, about 1 metre to the right of the first person)—whose lower bodies are truncated by the bottom edge of the frame. Across the five frames, the left person's mask expands and shifts slightly right as he steps closer and tilts his head forward and right, shifting from looking toward the camera wearer in frame 1 to looking down toward the space between himself and the right person in frames 2 through 5, while the right person faces toward the camera wearer and raises both bent arms to chest height within their own arm's reach in frames 3 to 5. This map provides crisp 2D silhouettes for both individuals despite the motion blur and privacy blurring over the right person's torso and head in the RGB image, and shows the left person gradually occluding the rectangular object behind his head and shoulders. However, the segmentation map is unreliable for background layout and object classes: it misclassifies the bright kitchen window in frame 1 and the upper-left white wall cabinet in frames 2, 3, and 5 as a "tv" (and drops that mask completely in frame 4), swaps the instance colour IDs of the two people in frame 3, and fails to segment the rest of the room, the hanging lamps, or the camera wearer's own right arm entering within 0.5 metres in the bottom-right of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks only the upper-body skeleton and head keypoints of the person on the left (~2.8 metres away in frame 1, approaching to ~1.8 metres by frame 5), showing his torso facing mostly toward the camera wearer and angled slightly right while his lower body below the hips is out of view at the bottom of the frame. In frame 1, his facial keypoints are clustered facing the camera wearer and both arms hang straight down at his sides within reach of the counter area beside him; from frame 2 to frame 5, his shoulder line rises and widens in the image as he steps forward, and his facial keypoints shift toward the right side of his head cluster as he turns his gaze downward and to his right, away from the camera wearer. The skeleton keypoints make the exact tilt of his shoulder axis and the downward-right rotation of his head explicit across the sequence even against the dark, shadowed kitchen background in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is severely incomplete and unreliable elsewhere: after frame 1 it loses his hip keypoints and lower arms (omitting his left upper arm entirely in frame 2), detects no hand skeletons (magenta) in any frame, and completely fails to detect the blurred person standing 1.5 to 1.8 metres away on the right or the camera wearer's own right hand and arm entering in the bottom-right foreground of frame 5.
